title: Freelance Client Onboarding Kit
description: Start every client project clearly: intake questionnaire, scope of work template with a completed example, five onboarding emails, a 30-minute kickoff agenda, a step-by-step checklist and a change request log to stop scope creep.

files.README.md:
# Freelance Client Onboarding Kit

Start every new client the same clear way: the right questions before you quote, a scope both of you sign off on, a kickoff call that sets the rules, and a simple log for every "small extra" that comes up later.

Good onboarding is the cheapest way to avoid the two things that cost freelancers the most: scope creep and late payment.

## What's inside

| File | Use it for |
|---|---|
| onboarding-checklist.md | The full sequence from first enquiry to work starting. Tick it off for every client. |
| client-intake-questionnaire.md | Questions to send (or ask on a call) before you quote. |
| scope-of-work-template.md | A fill-in scope of work, plus a completed example. |
| welcome-emails.md | Five ready-to-send emails: discovery, proposal, welcome, kickoff recap, and change request. |
| kickoff-call-agenda.md | A 30-minute agenda that covers everything people forget to agree. |
| change-request-log.csv | One row per change the client asks for once work has started. Open in Excel, Google Sheets or Numbers. |

## Quick start (20 minutes)

1. Read **onboarding-checklist.md** once, start to finish, so you know the order.
2. Copy **client-intake-questionnaire.md** into a doc or email. Delete questions that don't apply to your work and add two of your own.
3. Read the completed example in **scope-of-work-template.md**, then save the blank version as your own template.
4. Put your name, services and links into the brackets in **welcome-emails.md** now, so each email is ready next time.
5. Open **change-request-log.csv**, delete the example rows, and save a copy per client.

## For every new client

| Stage | What you do | File |
|---|---|---|
| Enquiry | Reply within one working day, send the intake questions | welcome-emails.md (email 1), client-intake-questionnaire.md |
| Before quoting | Read their answers, short discovery call if needed | client-intake-questionnaire.md |
| Proposal | Fill in the scope of work and send it with your price | scope-of-work-template.md, welcome-emails.md (email 2) |
| Signed | Send the welcome email, invoice the deposit | welcome-emails.md (email 3) |
| Kickoff | Run the call, send the recap the same day | kickoff-call-agenda.md, welcome-emails.md (email 4) |
| During the work | Log every change request before saying yes | change-request-log.csv, welcome-emails.md (email 5) |

## Pairs well with

The Freelancer Get-Paid Kit (invoice tracker, payment reminders and payment terms) picks up where this kit ends: once the work is delivered and the invoice goes out.

## A note on contracts

The scope of work in this kit describes the job. It is not a full contract. For larger projects, use it alongside a written agreement that covers payment, ownership, liability and cancellation, and get it checked by someone qualified where you work. Nothing in this kit is legal advice.

## Tips

- Send the intake questions before any call. People who won't answer ten questions are rarely good clients.
- Price only after you have answers to the "Budget and timing" and "What done looks like" questions.
- Don't start work until the scope is approved in writing and the deposit has arrived. An email reply saying "Approved" is better than nothing.
- When a change comes in, log it first and reply second. It turns "can you just..." into a clear decision for the client.
files.onboarding-checklist.md:
# Client onboarding checklist

Copy this for each new client. Work top to bottom. Each stage has a clear "done" line: don't move on until it's true.

Client: ______________________   Project: ______________________   Date of first contact: __________

---

## 1. First enquiry (same or next working day)

- [ ] Replied within one working day (welcome-emails.md, email 1)
- [ ] Sent the intake questionnaire
- [ ] Noted where the lead came from (referral, website, social, repeat client)
- [ ] Checked basic fit: is this work you do, in a timeframe you can meet?

**Done when:** they have your questions and know what happens next.

## 2. Discovery (before any price)

- [ ] Intake answers received and read
- [ ] Gaps listed: what's still unclear about scope, timing or budget?
- [ ] Discovery call booked if needed (keep it to 20-30 minutes)
- [ ] Identified who makes the final decision and who approves invoices
- [ ] Checked for red flags (see bottom of this file)

**Done when:** you could explain the project back to them in three sentences and they'd agree.

## 3. Proposal and scope

- [ ] Scope of work filled in (scope-of-work-template.md)
- [ ] Deliverables listed one by one, each with what's included
- [ ] "Not included" section filled in. This is the one that prevents scope creep.
- [ ] Number of revision rounds stated
- [ ] Timeline with dates, including the dates you need things from them
- [ ] Price, deposit and payment schedule stated
- [ ] Proposal sent with an expiry date (welcome-emails.md, email 2)
- [ ] Follow-up date in your calendar (3-5 working days later)

**Done when:** the scope and price are in their inbox with a clear way to say yes.

## 4. Signed and paid

- [ ] Scope approved in writing (signature or a clear email reply)
- [ ] Contract signed, if you use one for this size of project
- [ ] Deposit invoice sent
- [ ] Deposit received. **Work starts after this, not before.**
- [ ] Client added to your invoice tracker
- [ ] Project folder created with a copy of the approved scope

**Done when:** you have written approval and the deposit is in your account.

## 5. Welcome and kickoff

- [ ] Welcome email sent (welcome-emails.md, email 3)
- [ ] Kickoff call booked within a week of signing
- [ ] Asked for every file, login and asset you need, with a due date
- [ ] Kickoff call held (kickoff-call-agenda.md)
- [ ] Recap email sent the same day (welcome-emails.md, email 4)
- [ ] All key dates in your calendar: their deadlines and yours

**Done when:** both of you have the same written list of dates, contacts and next steps.

## 6. During the work

- [ ] Change request log created for this client (change-request-log.csv)
- [ ] Every new request logged before you reply
- [ ] Changes outside scope priced and approved in writing before you start them
- [ ] Short status update sent at least once a week on longer projects
- [ ] Milestone invoices sent on the day each milestone is reached

**Done when:** the work is delivered, approved, and the final invoice is out.

---

## Red flags to notice early

None of these mean "say no" on their own, but two or more together are worth a pause.

- Won't share a budget range, even a rough one
- Wants work started before anything is agreed in writing
- Asks for a free sample or "test" piece of the real project
- Can't say who makes the final decision
- Deadline is very short and the reason is vague
- Talks badly about every previous freelancer they've hired
- Pushes back hard on a deposit for a first project
files.client-intake-questionnaire.md:
# Client intake questionnaire

Send this before a call or a quote. It saves you an hour of back-and-forth and shows the client you take the work seriously.

**How to use it:** paste the questions into an email or a shared doc. Delete any that don't fit your work and add a few that do. Ten to fifteen questions is plenty. Keep the intro line: it tells the client why you're asking.

---

## Intro to paste above the questions

> Thanks for getting in touch. To give you an accurate quote and timeline, I'd like to understand the project a bit better. Could you answer the questions below? Short answers are fine, and "not sure yet" is a perfectly good answer too.

---

## About you

1. What does your business or organisation do, in a sentence or two?
2. Who are your customers or audience?
3. Who will I be working with day to day, and who makes the final decision?
4. Who should invoices go to (name and email)? Do you need a purchase order number on invoices?

## The project

5. What do you need, in your own words?
6. Why now? What prompted this project?
7. What problem should this solve, or what should it make possible?
8. Is there anything existing I'll be building on or replacing? (Files, a current website, earlier versions, brand guidelines.)
9. Are there examples you like, from anywhere? What do you like about them?
10. Is there anything you definitely don't want?

## What done looks like

11. How will you know this project has been a success?
12. What exactly do you expect to receive at the end? (For example: file types, number of pages, number of designs, a working site, a written report.)
13. Who else needs to review or approve the work before it's final?

## Budget and timing

14. Do you have a budget range for this project? A rough range is fine and helps me suggest the right option.
15. Is there a fixed deadline, and what happens if it moves?
16. Are there dates you or your team are unavailable?

## Working together

17. How do you prefer to communicate: email, calls, a messaging app?
18. How quickly can you usually give feedback on drafts? (A day, a few days, a week?)
19. Have you worked with a freelancer on something like this before? What went well, and what didn't?
20. Anything else I should know?

---

## Reading the answers

Before you quote, check you can answer each of these from what they sent:

| Question | Where it comes from |
|---|---|
| What exactly am I delivering? | 5, 12 |
| How will they judge it? | 7, 11 |
| Who signs off, and who pays? | 3, 4, 13 |
| Can I do it by their date? | 15, 16, 18 |
| Does their budget fit my price? | 14 |
| Will working together be smooth? | 17, 18, 19 |

If you can't answer one, ask about it on a short call or by email before you send a price.

## If they won't share a budget

Offer two or three options at different prices instead:

> Thanks, that's helpful. Projects like this usually fall into three sizes. A smaller version covering [core deliverable] is around [price]. The version most clients choose, which adds [extra], is around [price]. A full version with [extras] is around [price]. Which of these is closest to what you had in mind?

This gets you a budget signal without forcing them to name a number first.

# Scope of work

Part 1 is the blank template. Part 2 is a completed example for a small website project, so you can see the level of detail that works.

Write the scope in plain language. If a client can't tell from this page whether something is included, it will turn into an argument later.

---

# Part 1: Blank template

**Scope of work: [Project name]**

Prepared for: [Client name, business name]
Prepared by: [Your name, business name]
Date: [date]
Valid until: [date, usually 14-30 days later]

## 1. Project summary
[Two or three sentences: what you're making, for whom, and why.]

## 2. Deliverables
| # | Deliverable | What's included | Format |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | [name] | [details: quantity, size, length] | [file type or medium] |
| 2 | [name] | [details] | [format] |
| 3 | [name] | [details] | [format] |

## 3. Not included
The following are not part of this project. They can be quoted separately if needed.
- [item]
- [item]
- [item]

## 4. Revisions
This project includes [2] rounds of revisions on [each deliverable / the full set]. A round means one set of combined feedback, sent together. Further rounds are charged at [rate] per [hour / round].

## 5. What I need from you
| What | By when |
|---|---|
| [content, files, logins, access] | [date] |
| Feedback on first draft | Within [3] working days of receiving it |
| Final approval | Within [3] working days of final draft |

If these arrive late, the delivery dates below will move by the same amount.

## 6. Timeline
| Milestone | Date |
|---|---|
| Project starts (after deposit received) | [date] |
| [Milestone] | [date] |
| [Milestone] | [date] |
| Final delivery | [date] |

## 7. Price and payment
| Item | Amount |
|---|---|
| [Deliverable or phase] | [amount] |
| [Deliverable or phase] | [amount] |
| **Total** | **[amount]** |

Payment schedule: [50]% deposit before work starts, [50]% on final delivery. Invoices are due within [14] days.

## 8. Changes
Requests outside this scope will be logged and quoted before work on them begins. Nothing extra is charged without your written approval.

## 9. Approval
To approve this scope, reply "Approved" to this email or sign below.

Client: ____________________   Date: __________

[Your name]: ____________________   Date: __________

---

# Part 2: Completed example

**Scope of work: Bakery website refresh**

Prepared for: Sam Lee, Example Bakery
Prepared by: Alex Rivera, Rivera Web Studio
Date: 3 November 2026
Valid until: 17 November 2026

## 1. Project summary
A refreshed five-page website for Example Bakery that works well on phones, shows the weekly menu clearly, and makes it easy to place a pre-order for collection. The current site is hard to update and most visitors leave from the home page.

## 2. Deliverables
| # | Deliverable | What's included | Format |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Page design | Designs for 5 pages: Home, Menu, Pre-order, About, Contact. Phone and desktop versions. | Shared design file and PDF |
| 2 | Built website | The 5 pages built on the client's existing website platform, using the approved designs | Live website |
| 3 | Menu page set-up | Menu page set up so the client can change items and prices without help | Live website |
| 4 | Handover | One 45-minute video call showing how to edit pages and the menu, plus a one-page written guide | Call + PDF |

## 3. Not included
- Writing page copy (client supplies all text; light editing for length is included)
- Photography (client supplies photos; I'll resize and optimise them)
- Online payments or a full online shop
- Logo or brand design
- Ongoing updates after handover (available at the hourly rate below)
- Search engine advertising or social media set-up

## 4. Revisions
This project includes 2 rounds of revisions on the designs and 1 round on the built website. A round means one set of combined feedback, sent together. Further rounds are charged at $60 per hour.

## 5. What I need from you
| What | By when |
|---|---|
| Text for all 5 pages | 10 November |
| 10-20 photos of products and the shop | 10 November |
| Login to the website platform | 6 November |
| Feedback on designs | Within 3 working days of receiving them |
| Feedback on built site | Within 3 working days of receiving it |

If these arrive late, the delivery dates below will move by the same amount.

## 6. Timeline
| Milestone | Date |
|---|---|
| Project starts (after deposit received) | 5 November |
| First designs sent | 14 November |
| Designs approved | 21 November |
| Built site ready for review | 3 December |
| Final delivery and handover call | 10 December |

## 7. Price and payment
| Item | Amount |
|---|---|
| Design (5 pages, phone and desktop) | $900 |
| Build and menu set-up | $1,100 |
| Handover call and guide | $150 |
| **Total** | **$2,150** |

Payment schedule: 50% deposit ($1,075) before work starts, 50% ($1,075) on final delivery. Invoices are due within 14 days.

## 8. Changes
Requests outside this scope will be logged and quoted before work on them begins. Nothing extra is charged without your written approval.

## 9. Approval
To approve this scope, reply "Approved" to this email or sign below.

---

## Why the example works

- **Each deliverable has a number.** "5 pages" and "one 45-minute call" can't be stretched.
- **"Not included" names the likely extras.** Copywriting, photos and online payments are the three things a bakery client is most likely to assume are included.
- **Client deadlines are written down.** When the photos arrive late, the delivery date moves, and nobody has to argue about it.
- **A revision round is defined.** "One set of combined feedback" stops a stream of single comments, each treated as a new round.
files.welcome-emails.md:
# Onboarding emails

Five emails that carry a client from first enquiry to the middle of the project. Replace everything in [brackets]. Keep them short: clients read them on phones.

---

## Email 1: Reply to a new enquiry

**Subject:** Re: [their subject] — next steps

Hi [name],

Thanks for getting in touch about [project in their words]. It sounds like a good fit for the kind of work I do.

To give you an accurate quote and timeline, I've put a few questions below. Short answers are fine, and "not sure yet" is a perfectly good answer.

[paste intake questions]

Once I have your answers, I'll come back within [2] working days with either a proposal or a couple of follow-up questions. If it's easier to talk it through, you can book a 20-minute call here: [your booking method].

Best,
[your name]

---

## Email 2: Sending the proposal

**Subject:** Proposal: [project name] for [business name]

Hi [name],

Thanks for your answers, they were really helpful. Attached is the scope of work for [project name].

In short:
- **What you get:** [one-line summary of deliverables]
- **Timeline:** start on [date], final delivery by [date]
- **Investment:** [total], with a [50]% deposit to begin

The "Not included" section lists a few things that are often assumed to be part of projects like this, so it's worth a quick look.

This proposal is valid until [date]. To go ahead, just reply "Approved" and I'll send the deposit invoice and a welcome pack. If anything doesn't look right, tell me and I'll adjust it.

Best,
[your name]

---

## Email 3: Welcome (after approval)

**Subject:** Welcome aboard — [project name]

Hi [name],

I'm glad we're working together on [project name]. Here's what happens next:

1. **Deposit invoice** is attached. Work starts as soon as it's paid.
2. **Kickoff call:** could you pick a 30-minute slot in the next week? [booking method or two suggested times]
3. **What I need from you** (by [date]):
   - [item]
   - [item]
   - [item]

**How we'll work together**
- I'll send a short update every [Friday] so you always know where things stand.
- Email is the best way to reach me. I reply within [one working day], Monday to Friday.
- Feedback works best as one combined list per round, so nothing gets missed.

Looking forward to getting started.

Best,
[your name]

---

## Email 4: Kickoff recap (same day as the call)

**Subject:** Kickoff recap: [project name]

Hi [name],

Thanks for the call today. Here's a summary so we're both working from the same list.

**Agreed**
- [decision]
- [decision]

**Key dates**
| What | Who | When |
|---|---|---|
| [item] | [you / client] | [date] |
| [item] | [you / client] | [date] |
| First draft | [your name] | [date] |

**Contacts**
- Day-to-day: [name, email]
- Final approval: [name]
- Invoices: [name, email]

**Open questions**
- [question] — [who will answer, by when]

If I've got anything wrong, reply and I'll update it.

Best,
[your name]

---

## Email 5: Responding to a change request

Use this whenever a request falls outside the approved scope. Log it in change-request-log.csv first.

**Subject:** Re: [their subject] — change request [CR-number]

Hi [name],

Thanks for this, [the idea] would work well.

It's outside the scope we agreed, so I've logged it as change request [CR-number]. Here's what it would involve:

- **What:** [short description]
- **Extra cost:** [amount]
- **Effect on timeline:** [none / final delivery moves to date]

Reply "Approved" and I'll add it in. Or, if you'd rather keep to the original budget, we can leave it for now or swap it for [something in scope of similar size].

Best,
[your name]

---

## Tone tips

- Say what happens next in every email. Clients relax when they know the next step.
- Name dates, not durations. "By Friday 14 November" beats "within a week".
- When saying no to something free, offer a choice: pay for it, swap it, or save it for later.
files.kickoff-call-agenda.md:
# Kickoff call agenda (30 minutes)

A kickoff call isn't a chat. Its job is to turn the approved scope into a shared plan, and to agree the things that cause trouble later if nobody says them out loud.

Send the agenda with the calendar invite. Take notes straight into the recap email (welcome-emails.md, email 4) during the call, and send it the same day.

---

## Before the call (10 minutes)

- [ ] Re-read their intake answers and the approved scope
- [ ] List everything you still need from them, with dates
- [ ] Write down your top 3 questions
- [ ] Have the recap email open and ready to fill in

---

## Agenda

### 1. Goals (5 minutes)
- "In your words, what does a great result look like?"
- "What would make you say this project was a waste?"
- Write their answers down word for word. You'll use them to check drafts later.

### 2. Scope walk-through (7 minutes)
- Go through each deliverable in the scope, one line at a time.
- Read the "Not included" list aloud. Ask: "Is there anything here you were expecting me to do?"
- Confirm the number of revision rounds and what a round means.

### 3. Dates and dependencies (6 minutes)
- Confirm every date in the timeline.
- Go through what you need from them and by when.
- Say clearly: "If these arrive late, the delivery date moves by the same amount."
- Ask about holidays, launches or busy periods on their side.

### 4. People and communication (5 minutes)
- Who gives feedback? Who has the final say? Are they the same person?
- Who handles invoices?
- Preferred channel, and expected reply times on both sides.
- How and when you'll send updates.

### 5. Feedback process (4 minutes)
- Feedback arrives as one combined list per round.
- Feedback is due within [3] working days of receiving a draft.
- "Can you tell me what's not working, rather than how to fix it? That helps me find the best solution."

### 6. Next steps (3 minutes)
- Read back the actions, owners and dates.
- Confirm you'll send the recap today.
- Ask: "Is there anything I haven't asked that I should know?"

---

## Questions worth asking on every kickoff

- "Who else will see this before it's final, and what do they care about?"
- "Is there anything that's been tried before and didn't work?"
- "What's the one thing you most want me to get right?"

## After the call

- [ ] Recap email sent (same day)
- [ ] All dates in your calendar, including the ones the client owns
- [ ] Reminders set two days before each client deadline
- [ ] Change request log created for this client
